title: Harold Flood's band and leaving for the East
summary: Dance mentions drummer Harold Flood. Thomas mentions a gig on Bleak Street and a telegram from Burke Bailey about a walkathon, then left Abernathy to head east.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You were with drummer Harold Flood in Milwaukee ...
... WATCH this guy ... that's a funny scene. Flood worked with a man called, in Grant Moore's band. He got a gig
on (Bleak) Street and it was a very nice little group there. You'd better turn this off.
Well, where was this Harold Flood's band playing?
Al Flood's band was playing at Street right around the corner from the restaurant. with
Well, when did you work for him?

When I was getting ready, I left Abernathy and I was getting ready to come east. I had a telegram from Burke Bailey, it must have been, to come to join a walk-a-thon -- they had a thing called a walk-a-thon in those days. And they wanted me to (..?)

Burke Bailey I told El, El I've got to make it now. I can't, you know. We had a tremendous band out there, I thought. But, it's time for me to go so I told him, well, I'm going. He was always very thoughtful. A very thoughtful musician. So I came to Camden, New Jersey.
